newsitem.title: USA: Petroecuador signs 3 term deals for Oriente crude.
newsitem.headline: Petroecuador signs 3 term deals for Oriente crude.

text.p: Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador signed three new term contracts for Oriente crude oil, and concurrently raised its formula price for all customers by 30 cents a barrel, trade sources said on Thursday.

France's Total Petroleum, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) and Tevier, a company associated with Swiss trading house Glencore, each signed one-year contracts for 12,000 barrels per day (bpd) beginning July 1.

The contracts formerly were in the hands of PMI, the trading arm of Mexico's state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), and Totisa, a subsidiary of Ecuadoran trading house Tripetrol. These contracts recently lapsed.
Petroecuador directly negotiated the new deals, using the 30-cent formula price increase as leverage, the sources said.

Petroecuador currently has 12 term customers for Oriente, including the three new clients. The country exports around 240,000 bpd, mostly to the United States.
Oriente is a medium-gravity crude with around one percent sulfur. The grade loads at the Ecuadoran port of Esmeraldas.
